connector: The boys got out of the sewer, and the outlaws met the brewery rats. Today is the last chapter. The prince says they are going back to the castle. Watch his face when he tells Betsy and Captain Nips to turn Jemmy in.

a.raw: they're waiting for us at the gate said jemmy
a.fixed: “They’re waiting for us at the gate,” said Jemmy.
a.why: The words Jemmy says go inside quotation marks. They’re starts the sentence, so it gets a capital T. A comma goes inside the closing quotation mark. Jemmy is a name, so it gets a capital J. A period ends it.

b.raw: the reward is yours said the king
b.fixed: “The reward is yours,” said the king.
b.why: The words the king says go inside quotation marks. The starts the sentence, so it gets a capital T. A comma goes inside the closing quotation mark. A period ends it.

mfill1.h1: Say re, then read. Push them together.
mfill1.why: re + read = reread: to read again.

mfill2.h1: Say un, then fair. Push them together.

mfill3.h1: Say pre, then heat. Push them together.
mfill3.why: pre + heat = preheat: to heat before.

mfill4.h1: Say dis, then trust. Push them together.
mfill4.why: dis + trust = distrust: to not trust.

mfill5.h1: Say mis, then spell. Keep both s’s.
mfill5.why: mis + spell = misspell: to spell wrong. It has two s’s.

items.title: Front word parts
items.q: Jemmy had to rethink what the prince was doing. What does rethink mean?
items.why: re means again. Rethink means think again.

miss.1: Before would be pre. Which word part is at the front of rethink?

items.title: Front word parts
items.why: dis can mean not. Dishonest means not honest.

miss.0: Again would be re. Which word part is at the front of dishonest?

items.title: Front word parts
items.q: Before a big test, a teacher may give a pretest. What is a pretest?
items.why: pre means before. A pretest comes before the real test.

miss.1: Wrong would be mis. Which word part is at the front of pretest?

items.title: Front word parts
items.q: The prince promised not to misbehave. What does misbehave mean?
items.why: mis means wrong or badly. Misbehave means behave badly.

miss.0: Again would be re. Which word part is at the front of misbehave?

items.title: Sound-alike words
items.q: The king looked at the ___ boys.
items.why: two is the number 2: two boys.

miss.0: too means also or more than enough. Here you need a number.

items.title: Sound-alike words
items.why: to sits in front of a verb: to run.

miss.1: two is a number. Here the word sits in front of run.

items.title: Sound-alike words
items.q: The golden doors opened, and ___ sat the king.

miss.0: their shows belonging. Here you need a place.

items.title: Prepositional phrases
items.q: The prince stood beside Jemmy. Which word is the preposition?
items.why: beside sits in front of Jemmy and tells where.

miss.1: stood is what the prince did. Look for the word in front of Jemmy.

the big lesson a story teaches. You can say it in one sentence.
a word part at the front of a word that changes its meaning, like re in rebuild
words that sound the same but mean different things and are spelled differently, like to, two, and too
a group of words that starts with a preposition and ends on a noun, like under the straw
writing about a thing as if it were a person, like a sea that crawls
the last sentence of a paragraph. It says your big idea in a new way.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. This is it, the very last chapter. The boys are out of the sewer, and the prince says, We’re going back to the castle. Jemmy has a price on his head! As you read, watch the prince’s face very closely.
transcripts.guide1: Word work. Today you’ll build five new words with front word parts, find the noun at the end of each phrase, and pick the right sound-alike word.
transcripts.guide2: Before you read: the prince does something that looks like a betrayal. Keep reading. Then the boys stand before the king. Listen for the promise the prince made.
transcripts.guide3: Today you write the middle of your comparison: one way the boys changed the same, and one way they changed differently.

notes.wordParts: These word parts go at the front of a word. re = again (rebuild), un = not (unhappy), pre = before (preview), dis = not (disagree), mis = wrong (misread).
notes.grammar: A prepositional phrase starts with a preposition and ends on a noun: through the fog. It can tell where, when, or how.
notes.spelling: Homophones sound the same but mean different things. to points (to the gate), two is the number 2, too means also or more than enough. their = belongs to them, there = a place, they’re = they are.
notes.wgrd: The theme is the big lesson a story wants you to take away.

Then she says how each boy changed in his own way. Now write one way they changed the same, and one way they changed differently.

items.t: Jemmy has a price on his head, but he follows the prince back toward the castle.
items.why: He is scared, and he goes anyway.

items.t: Betsy is told to turn Jemmy in, and she says, “I’ll do no such thing.”
items.why: She stands up for Jemmy, even when a boy says he is the prince.

items.t: When the prince says to turn him in, Jemmy thinks, Run for it.
